donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

votes.question: On Passage — National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes fiscal year 2027 military programs, troop levels, and related Energy Department national-security work. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.plain_language: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment prohibiting total federal expenditures for a year from exceeding the average annual federal receipts collected in the three prior years, adjusted for changes in the population of U.S. citizens and inflation. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7744)
votes.bill_title: Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill provides appropriations to the Department of Homeland Security for the remainder of FY2026. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7744)

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H R 7148)
votes.bill_title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026

posts.text:
Great visiting L2 Brands in Hanover!

The company traces its roots to 1992, when two law school roommates had an idea to make a better baseball cap. More than three decades later, that idea has grown into a successful business producing customized apparel and headwear for https://t.co/qlwYaKjbWp

On Veterans Day, we honor and thank the brave men and women who have worn our nation’s uniform and answered the call to serve.

Their service and sacrifice, along with the sacrifices made by their families, have helped preserve the freedoms we enjoy every day.

To all veterans across York and Lancaster counties and throughout our nation: Thank you for your service. We are forever grateful.

Congratulations to Leader @Jim_Jordan, @GOPMajorityWhip, Conference Chair @RepLisaMcClain, and the rest of the @HouseGOP  Leadership Team on your elections today! I I look forward to the work we’ll do as a united Republican Conference to deliver results for the American people.

World-class research, product development, and manufacturing are happening right here in York County at Adhesives Research in Glen Rock!

What began in a converted garage in 1961 has grown into an international company employing over 400 people. It has remained a family-owned business and is a great American success story that is a testament to the ingenuity happening right here in our communities.

Thank you to the entire Adhesives Research team for the behind-the-scenes tour and for sticking with and continuing to invest in York County!

October was a busy month across Lancaster and York counties!

From visiting local businesses and manufacturers to meeting with students, community leaders, and employers, I enjoyed hearing directly from the people of PA-11.

Catch up on these visits, my work in Washington, and how my office is helping constituents in my latest e-newsletter.

Read more: https://t.co/lqOgVGSK5a

Every day, first responders across Lancaster and York counties answer the call to help their neighbors in times of need.

On National First Responders Day, we recognize the firefighters, law enforcement officers, EMS personnel, emergency medical flight crews, dispatchers, and others who work to keep our communities safe.

Thank you for your courage, dedication, and service!

Great visiting Cleveland Brothers in Brownstown!

Now in its third generation of family leadership, with the fourth generation already involved, Cleveland Brothers supports businesses across our region with heavy equipment, rentals, parts, and service.

Thanks to the team for showing me around and for the work you do to keep our local economy moving!

There are AMAZING things happening at York Tech. I was grateful to visit their campus again to learn more about their programs which prepare students to succeed after graduation. I appreciated the opportunity to learn directly from students in the welding and precision machining programs. I'm grateful for the work of the administration and educators who are making a positive difference in York County.

Happy 100th Birthday to UPMC Hanover Hospital! In late October 1926, then Hanover General Hospital opened its doors to receive patients. THANK YOU to the dedicated physicians, nurses, and staff, have provided trusted medical care over the past century to the families who call https://t.co/NQiXMupxvH

Great day in Manheim last week! 

I enjoyed starting our visits with a luncheon and conversation with local elected officials from northern Lancaster County at Twisted Sisters Ice Cream and Handmade Chocolates, alongside State Rep. Mindy Fee.

We also visited Stiegel Glassworks 1976, Glasshouse Wineworks, and REO Manheim Marketplace, three local businesses that showcase Manheim’s unique character, rich history, and vibrant downtown.

Thank you to everyone who welcomed us! It’s always a pleasure to spend time with the people and small businesses helping our communities thrive.

Congratulations to the 35 newest American citizens from 16 different countries who took the Oath of Allegiance yesterday in York County!

A special congratulations to the Charles family, who our office had the privilege of assisting with a matter before U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

Becoming an American citizen is a meaningful milestone, and we wish all of our newest fellow Americans the very best as they begin this exciting new chapter!

Decisions on when to claim Social Security shouldn’t be made more confusing by government terminology.

My bipartisan Claiming Age Clarity Act has passed Congress and is headed to the President’s desk.

It will help Americans better understand their retirement benefits.

More from CNBC: https://t.co/u38p394k9f

$40 trillion in debt. More than $1 trillion a year just to pay the interest.

We know this path is unsustainable. The question is whether we choose to act now.

I joined the 584 Vetoes podcast to discuss the case for a bipartisan fiscal commission and a path toward getting our fiscal house in order.

🎧 https://t.co/nT4swgAIeU

From snack foods and farm equipment to advanced technology and structural steel fabrication, PA-11 makes things.

On Manufacturing Day, we celebrate the manufacturers and skilled workers who create good jobs and keep our local economy strong.

Proud of all that’s made right here in PA-11. 

#MFGDay26

Hi @alaborngaming1  -thank you for reaching out, and thank you for your service. While our office unfortunately isn’t able to directly resolve issues with https://t.co/N7OUmyexEB, we’d like to connect with you to better understand what you’re experiencing and see whether there may be another way we can assist. Please send us a direct message with the best way to reach you, and a member of our team will follow up.
Watch the press conference and learn more: https://t.co/dFjULw4u9v

61 historic artifacts connected to President James Buchanan’s family are back with their rightful owners.

These items had come to the Pennsylvania Treasury as unclaimed property, and yesterday I joined @PATreasurer at LancasterHistory for their return to the Buchanan family.

Thank you, Treasurer Garrity, for your tremendous work to return unclaimed property to Pennsylvanians across our Commonwealth.
Thank you to my colleague and lead sponsor of the legislation in the Senate, @SenBillCassidy, for his leadership on this bill!
More here: https://t.co/cfAgWa0hzg

🚨The Senate has passed bipartisan and commonsense legislation I’ve introduced with @RepDonBeyer to help America’s seniors make informed decisions when deciding to claim their Social Security benefits. The bill will now be sent to President Trump for his signature. https://t.co/olzdU9nA7y https://t.co/iN68ijLWPg

249 years ago today, Lancaster served as the capital of our young nation for one day.

On September 27, 1777, the Continental Congress convened in Lancaster after fleeing Philadelphia as British forces advanced. After meeting here, delegates traveled across the Susquehanna River to York, where Congress continued its work during a pivotal chapter of the American Revolution.

As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, we’re proud to remember the important role our communities played in our nation’s founding.

A great look at this history from @SmithsonianMag: https://t.co/K62fjnIYn6

Our $40T national debt is a serious challenge, but one we can still solve.

I joined @KurtCouchman of @AFPhq on @RepublicanStudy’s Right to the Point to discuss the need to change our fiscal trajectory.

Thanks @MatthewFoldi for the coverage:

https://t.co/OqKin7MuMa

Washington can debate whether it's a spending problem or a revenue problem.

It's a math problem.

We take in $5 trillion and spend $7 trillion. It's time to confront our nation's fiscal challenges and put America on a better trajectory. https://t.co/PfmRI5atGX
Wishing a meaningful Yom Kippur to all those observing in Pennsylvania’s 11th District and across the country. May this day of reflection and atonement bring peace and renewal.

Today is #NationalAppChallengeDay! STEM initiatives like the Congressional App Challenge are direct investments into the next generation of leaders and innovators. I encourage all young coders in the district to submit their apps by October 26. For more information, visit https://t.co/L4YpG3Vsvc

On this day in 1787, our Founders signed the United States Constitution in Philadelphia.

For more than two centuries, the Constitution has served as the foundation of our republic, protecting our liberties and ensuring our government remains accountable to “We the People.”

Happy Constitution Day!

Families and small businesses should not be forced to pay the enormous energy costs created by new data centers. Period. That’s why I voted for the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act.

The principle is simple: data centers should locate in communities that choose to host them, those communities should share in the economic benefits, and data centers should pay their own way.

Read my full statement: https://t.co/ZiF5Gyb9c1

A big thank you to Scott T. of Lititz and his colleagues from the American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network for visiting our Washington office to discuss federal funding for cancer research and bipartisan efforts to reduce barriers for patients enrolling in clinical trials.

I appreciated hearing their stories and perspectives, and discussing ways we can continue supporting patients and families impacted by cancer.

25 years later, I still remember exactly where I was on September 11, 2001, and the moment we realized our country was under attack.

We remember the nearly 3,000 innocent lives lost, the first responders who ran toward danger, the passengers and crew of Flight 93 who fought back here in Pennsylvania, and the servicemembers who answered our nation’s call.

I also remember what followed: Americans came together. We prayed together, supported one another and remembered that whatever our differences, we are Americans first.

As we mark 25 years since that tragic day, may we never forget the courage, service, faith and unity that followed.

Earlier this morning, preparations were underway at West Manheim Elementary School to mark the 25th anniversary of September 11.

Seeing 3,000 American flags across the school grounds is a powerful reminder of the lives lost on that tragic day and of our promise to never forget.

Thank you to the Exchange Club of Hanover and the many volunteers who worked to make this meaningful tribute possible.

Happy Labor Day! Today, we celebrate the workers who build, grow, make, serve, and strengthen our communities every day.

Wishing everyone across Pennsylvania’s 11th District a safe and enjoyable holiday! https://t.co/3sYWGizuA7

You never know where a good conversation might take place. This one happened inside a dumpster! 

I recently joined Todd and Alex of Sahd Metal Recycling for an episode of their Dumpster Talk podcast to talk about our economy, public service, my experience as a small business owner, and more.

Stay tuned for the premiere of our conversation next week!

There's a reason Hanover is known as the Snack Capital of the World!

I recently visited G&S Foods and Campbell's Hanover snack facility to see firsthand the innovation and manufacturing that help make our community famous for snacks enjoyed across the country.

From pretzels and chips to some of America's most recognizable snack brands, Hanover has a proud history of making great things. Thanks to both teams for having me and for continuing that tradition right here in York County!

162 thousand jobs created is good news, a growing economy is essential to getting our fiscal house in order. But we can’t put the burden of growing our economy solely on American workers and businesses while the federal government continues adding trillions to the debt. https://t.co/XQf3zoze90

Governor Shapiro warned this week that there are ‘real life consequences’ to scaring people with misinformation rather than providing unbiased information from medical professionals. Yet he rushed to hold a press conference, attack the Trump administration, and accuse others of spreading misinformation before Pennsylvanians had the full facts.
 
We now know that the Lancaster County Coroner has determined that measles neither caused nor contributed to the death of the newborn identified by the Commonwealth as one of two ‘measles-associated’ deaths. The Shapiro administration has still provided virtually no information about the circumstances surrounding the second death.
 
These deaths are tragic for the families who lost loved ones. Using their deaths for political purposes before all the facts were known is shameful.
 
Governor Shapiro was awfully quick to get in front of the cameras and assign blame. He should be just as quick to give Pennsylvanians the facts. His administration needs to explain what it knew when these deaths were announced, why they were characterized as ‘measles-associated,’ and what occurred in the second case.
